knowledgePattern: Compare a local maximum with a stronger derivative condition
solution:
Write the polynomial near zero as y=a0+a1x+a2x2+x3r(x). Condition Q gives a1=0 and 2a2<−1. Thus y′=x(2a2+xs(x)) for another polynomial s.

The bracket is negative sufficiently close to zero because its value at zero is negative. The derivative is therefore positive just to the left of zero and negative just to the right. Hence Q implies P.

Conversely y=−x4 has a local maximum at zero but y′′(0)=0, so it does not satisfy Q. Thus P is necessary but not sufficient for Q. Answer B.

hints.title: Write both implication directions
hints.body: Treat the local-maximum statement and the derivative statement as two separate conditions and identify which implication each classification asks you to prove.
hints.recap: Necessary and sufficient test opposite directions between a fixed condition and target.
hints.pitfall: A derivative condition can be stronger than the feature it guarantees.
hints.pause: Test each direction and decide whether it can be proved or needs a counterexample.

hints.title: Inspect the first nonconstant terms
hints.body: Write the polynomial using its constant, linear and quadratic terms, with the remaining higher powers grouped together. Translate the derivative data into coefficient information.
hints.recap: Differentiate a polynomial term by term, and differentiate twice before evaluating a second derivative.
hints.pitfall: A zero derivative alone does not settle whether a local maximum occurs.
hints.pause: Use the resulting derivative to check the signs immediately on each side of zero.
